content:
When Apple finally responded to the surge in memory and other component costs, its stance was anything but gentle. Some price increases exceeded fifty percent, while upgrades to memory and storage on certain configurations nearly doubled in price.

These higher price points are expected to persist for years, and may even become permanent...

9to5Mac readers were already skeptical about whether Apple would lower prices once the component shortages eased. Over two-thirds of respondents indicated they expected these price hikes to be permanent.

Subsequently, analyst reports suggested that supply chain prices would not see significant improvement until 2028, and even if they did ease by then, the reductions would be quite limited. The current high pricing policy appears set to remain for at least several years, and may never return to previous levels.

If this is indeed the case, how would you respond? Would you grit your teeth and continue purchasing Apple products at the same frequency? Or would you reduce the number or frequency of your purchases? Or would you take other approaches, such as opting for more affordable models, buying refurbished units, or waiting for discounts?

Feel free to participate in our poll and share your thoughts in the comments. The poll allows multiple selections so you can express multiple shifts in your purchasing habits at once.
